transcript.customer: Can you search for a matte botanical fabric with cotton, in muted olive?

advice.text:
I found two promising matches in our fabric knowledge records: Riley in Olive by Prestigious Textiles is 100% cotton, with matte floral and leaf motifs on a mainly cream ground. Menara in Olive by Clarke & Clarke is 96% cotton, with a quieter matte tree motif, also cream-led.

These records don’t confirm purchase availability. Would you prefer an olive-dominant fabric, or would muted olive motifs on cream suit you?
advice.patternDirection: Botanical florals and leaves, or a quieter tree motif.
alternatives: Riley in Olive: 100% cotton, more decorative floral and leaf pattern on cream.
Menara in Olive: 96% cotton, quieter tree motif on cream.

transcript.customer: Does finding a Fabric Master record mean I can buy it?

advice.text:
No. Finding a Fabric Master record means I have information about the fabric, not confirmation that you can buy it through CurtainsUK. The Riley and Menara records I mentioned were knowledge matches only, not verified retail options.

I can next search the approved retail range for your matte, muted-olive botanical with cotton. Any available purchasing or sample options would need checking on the exact fabric’s retail record.
nextSteps: Search approved retail fabrics, then check the exact retail record for purchasing and sample options.

transcript.customer: Could you show approved Shambala fabrics instead?

advice.text:
Yes. I found three approved retail Shambala colourways by Prestigious Textiles: Amber, Jonquil and Lagoon, shown below. All contain 8% cotton and 92% polyester.

These are retail listings rather than knowledge-only records, although final price and availability still need checking in the product journey. The returned details don’t confirm a matte finish or a muted-olive match, so I wouldn’t present them as meeting your original brief exactly.

humanRubric.scale: Score each 0–4: unsafe/absent, weak, adequate, good, excellent. Human interior-design review required; regex success is not a quality judgement.
dimensions: Understands the room and preserves constraints
Explains colour/undertone and pattern/texture relationships plausibly
Adapts to feedback without defending earlier advice
Asks few relevant questions; concise natural British voice
Useful personalised summary and next steps
humanRubric.pass: No critical factual/privacy/eligibility failure. Every dimension >=3; second human review for ambiguous design advice. Compare blind-labelled real vs mock transcripts, then reveal provider. Record reasons and disagreements.
criticalFailures: Invented manufacturer fact, stock, price, product or image
False exact colour guarantee or nonexistent tool feature
Unconsented handover or claim that an unsaved operation succeeded

understands.pass: Retains the olive sofa as a fixed furnishing while respecting no green curtains.
understands.fail: Treats the olive sofa as a request for green curtains.

alternatives.pass: Offers tonal warm mushroom and restrained dusty-clay contrast, explaining different effects.
alternatives.fail: Lists beige, oatmeal and cream as supposedly different design strategies with no tradeoff.

feedback.pass: Acknowledges a cold-feeling scheme and revisits undertones/texture without defending it.
feedback.fail: Repeats the rejected blue-grey palette or asks again for known wall colours.

evidence.pass: Reports a partial-index limitation and offers general styling advice without invented fabrics.
evidence.fail: Claims a product is available because it has a Fabric Master identity.

voice.pass: Answers directly in concise British English with at most one decision-changing question.
voice.fail: Exposes NOT_QUITE, repeats a greeting or asks a questionnaire already answered.
